findings.evidence: Lines 600-618: `private theorem eLpNorm_toReal_eq_of_ae_lt_top {g : E → ℝ≥0∞} (hg : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, g x < ∞) : eLpNorm (fun x => (g x).toReal) p μ = eLpNorm g p μ`, then `theorem eLpNorm_maximalFunction_toReal_eq ... := eLpNorm_toReal_eq_of_ae_lt_top hM`. Mathlib has no `eLpNorm`-level toReal lemma (only the `p = 1` case `mem_L1_toReal_of_lintegral_ne_top`, Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Function/L1Space/Integrable.lean:919), so the general form is the one worth exporting.
findings.fix: Drop `private` from `eLpNorm_toReal_eq_of_ae_lt_top` and delete `eLpNorm_maximalFunction_toReal_eq`; call the general lemma directly at line 628 and in the module docstring.
findings.issue: `eLpNorm_maximalFunction_toReal_eq` is a strictly less general restatement of the private `eLpNorm_toReal_eq_of_ae_lt_top` (its proof is literally `eLpNorm_toReal_eq_of_ae_lt_top hM`): the general statement about any `g : E → ℝ≥0∞` is the reusable one, and specialising to `maximalFunction μ f` saves the caller nothing — the hypothesis and conclusion are the same after unfolding. The exported API is therefore the special case only.

findings.evidence: Lines 573-577 and 622-629 carry `(hp_top : p ≠ ∞)`; line 584-586 shows the `p = ∞` argument already written out: `(maximalFunction_le_eLpNormEssSup μ f x).trans_lt (by simpa only [eLpNorm_exponent_top] using hf_top.lt_top)`; `maximalFunction_le_eLpNormEssSup` at line 169 is stated for all `x` with no exponent hypothesis.
findings.fix: Delete `hp_top` from both: in `eLpNorm_maximalFunction_lt_top` add `rcases eq_or_ne p ∞` and settle the top case by `eLpNorm (M f) ∞ μ ≤ eLpNormEssSup f μ` via `maximalFunction_le_eLpNormEssSup` + `essSup_le_of_ae_le`; `memLp_maximalFunction_toReal` then goes through unchanged, since `eLpNorm_maximalFunction_toReal_eq` and `ae_maximalFunction_lt_top_of_eLpNorm_ne_top` both already hold at `p = ∞`. Update the docstrings and the `Main declarations` entry (line 98-101) accordingly.
findings.issue: `memLp_maximalFunction_toReal` and `eLpNorm_maximalFunction_lt_top` are restricted by `hp_top : p ≠ ∞`, but the classical statement is `1 < p ≤ ∞` and the `p = ∞` endpoint is a one-liner from lemmas in this file — the same gap the neighbouring `ae_maximalFunction_lt_top_of_eLpNorm_ne_top` already closes by covering `1 ≤ p ≤ ∞`. A caller with `f ∈ L^∞` cannot use either lemma.

summary: The general `ℝ≥0∞`→`ℝ` seminorm lemma is hidden behind `private` while only its maximal-function instance is exported, and the `MemLp`/finiteness results stop at `p ≠ ∞` although the `p = ∞` endpoint is already proved in this file.
